correctness.rationale: The conditional-on-clock survival probability is the product of reflection-principle survival factors Q_d(gap). Conditioning makes the two Brownian survival indicators independent, so differentiating the covariance at r=0 gives the integral of the two one-reset increments Delta. Histories with at least two resets have probability O((rt)^2), which controls the remainder because all conditional probabilities lie in [0,1]. For d1=d2 the covariance is Var(q_d(C)); the no-reset history and one-reset histories near an endpoint have different conditional survival values, so the variance is strictly positive. For d2^2>=6Dt, F_d2(s)=erfc(d2/sqrt(4Ds)) is convex on (0,t], implying Delta_d2(u)>0 and integral I2 >= t*c(d2)^2/3. The elementary erf bound gives integral Q_d1(u)Q_d1(t-u)du <= d1^2/D and Q_d1(t)>=d1/(e sqrt(pi D t)) when d1<2sqrt(Dt). The stated strict small-distance condition therefore makes J<0. Since J<0, the expansion forces negative covariance for sufficiently small positive r. CHECK.py is only a finite numerical illustration and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a mathematically motivated counterboundary to the intuition that a common external clock always creates positive survival association. It identifies a rigorous sign reversal caused solely by heterogeneous distances, relevant to joint nonarrival probabilities and variance models. The explicit all-parameter sufficient region and exact first-order mechanism are more than a numerical example; the proof states that the bound is sufficient rather than sharp.
